quotes.text: You can’t cancel an EPS refund after submitting it.
You must refund the customer using another method.
The customer has up to 1 hour to complete bank authorization

old_evidence.text: EPS payments can be refunded up to 180 days after the original payment date.
EPS redirects customers to their bank’s website to

findings: The November EPS page describes a single-use Austrian customer bank redirect: EUR presentment, instant provisional access, immediate payment result notification and standard payout schedule (new raw lines 5-15, 32-42, 113-137). The account can be in the listed 40 business locations and a merchant or Connect platform, while the EPS customer location is AT; the new page adds B2B/B2C and domestic/cross-border classifications, a 1.00 EUR minimum and possible post-activation account eligibility review (new raw lines 16-40). The May page also gave Austrian customers, EUR, redirect, immediate notification, 40 account locations, no recurring and standard payout (old raw lines 8-12, 14-54, 56-99). Neither account-list inclusion nor activation proves merchant-specific eligibility or a successful transaction.

The November payment flow spells out bank choice, redirect to bank login, customer-entered bank credentials, bank authorization within one hour, immediate result and optional return to the business (new raw lines 113-137). May documented the same redirect and six-stage flow without the one-hour limit (old raw lines 12, 113-132). The customer-facing result and optional browser return are distinct from merchant payout or Stripe balance settlement; the page's immediate confirmation and standard payout are separate states (new raw lines 12-14, 129-137). Current source lines 13, 17, 24 and concept lines 10, 14-25 summarize this core flow, though their wording should retain those state boundaries.

The 180-day refund submission window persists (old raw lines 154-156; new raw lines 57-68), while November adds full and multiple partial refunds, bank-dependent typical 1–3-day customer receipt with no guaranteed maximum, non-cancelability, separate-credit rather than reversal treatment, bank-statement labeling caveat, and status tracking through Refund.status and refund.updated/refund.failed events (new raw lines 57-78). A succeeded Refund object is a final outcome; a failed refund returns money to the Stripe balance and requires another customer refund method (new raw lines 76-78). Source lines 13 and 20 and concept line 28 accurately retain 180 days but lack these consequential qualifications.

EPS still excludes recurring and manual capture, and the November matrix explicitly excludes extended, incremental, decremental, re-authorizations, partial/multicapture/overcapture, SetupIntents, PaymentIntents with setup_future_usage and off-session payments (old raw lines 32-54; new raw lines 41-65, 105-110). It marks Checkout full page, Payment Links, embedded form, Payment Element, in-app, Billing, Invoicing, Radar and Connect supported, with Express Checkout Element, Payment Method Messaging Element, Customer Portal, Terminal and Managed Payments unsupported (new raw lines 86-112). The old product list was shorter, so its omissions are not blanket unsupported marks (old raw lines 101-111). Do not infer automatic recurring billing or subscription-mode Checkout from the Billing/Invoicing product names.

The May EPS page explicitly described Invoicing as invite-only (old raw lines 101-111), repeated by source line 22 and concept line 30. November marks Invoicing supported and places a send_invoice-only collection-method footnote after the product/API matrix, without repeating an invite restriction (new raw lines 96-112). This is a dated documentation conflict requiring reciprocal warning, not proof that invitations ceased for every account. The text capture does not unambiguously attach the footnote to one product row, so route-specific integration confirmation remains necessary; source and concept should not present the old invite-only claim as undated current eligibility.

Both captures say EPS's direct bank authentication avoids the standard chargeback dispute route (old raw lines 44-46, 150-152; new raw lines 63-65, 80-84). November clarifies that a customer who contacts the bank is directed to the merchant, who can issue a refund; it does not establish that all customer complaints are impossible (new raw lines 80-84). November adds non-card statement_descriptor behavior, account-level fallback, and destination-charge platform descriptor versus on_behalf_of connected-account descriptor (new raw lines 139-143). These are payment/Connect identity rules, not proof of the descriptor shown by a particular bank.

Current source-stripe-eps.md is a May-only summary with a May raw file (source lines 4-8, 11-28). It remains broadly right on Austria/EUR, single use, 180 days and no standard disputes but needs November provenance, the 1.00 EUR minimum, one-hour authorization, consequential refund failure and non-cancellation behavior, and dated Invoicing warning. The source's 'authentication prevents chargebacks' is directionally consistent with the raw's no-standard-dispute statement but should not imply zero fraud or every customer complaint impossible (old raw lines 150-152; new raw lines 80-84). Stripe index lines 275 and 752 and direct EPS concept lines 10-47 route the source and repeat the undated invite-only status in concept line 30.

The shared bank-redirects concept line 34 also repeats May's undated EPS Invoicing invite-only wording, while its line 33 presents EPS Subscriptions through send_invoice only; its May source lines 17-24 and underlying overview raw lines 24-34 establish the dated matrix and footnote. The November EPS-specific page marks Invoicing supported with an ambiguously attached send_invoice footnote but recurring payments unsupported (new raw lines 42, 96-112; old EPS raw lines 101-111). Warn reciprocally in the direct EPS and shared bank-redirect routes. The older per-invoice subscription route does not establish subscription-mode Checkout or automatic charge_automatically/off-session recurring EPS payments, and the November recurring-payment label does not itself negate that older manually sent invoice route.

Targeted retry personally reread new raw lines 36-44 and 94-114, old EPS raw lines 100-112, direct concept lines 23-32, shared bank-redirect concept lines 23-40, bank-redirect source lines 1-16 and 17-40, and historical bank-redirect raw lines 21-35 after checking unchanged pins and prior receipt/review; initial full-file ranges remain above.
substantive_changes: November explicitly documents account review/eligibility, B2B/B2C and cross-border classification, 1.00 EUR minimum, and one-hour bank authorization; these are new documented qualifications beyond May's Austrian customer/EUR/40-account-country and redirect overview (old raw lines 8-12, 14-99, 113-132; new raw lines 16-40, 113-137).

November expands refund lifecycle guidance to multiple partial refunds, non-cancelability, separate bank credit, typical-but-unguaranteed 1–3-day receipt, Refund.status/webhook outcomes and alternative refund on failure, while retaining the 180-day submission window (old raw lines 154-156; new raw lines 57-78).

The product/API matrix newly makes several supported and unsupported routes explicit; May's Invoicing invite-only footnote versus November's supported mark/send_invoice footnote is a dated documentation conflict, with no account-level rollout conclusion (old raw lines 101-111; new raw lines 86-112). The shared bank-redirects May matrix also lists EPS Subscriptions via send_invoice only, distinct from November's 'Recurring payments: Not supported' and off-session unsupported labels (raw/stripe-bank-redirects-2025.md lines 24-34; new raw lines 42, 105-112). May's old product-list omissions alone do not prove capability changes.
historical_claims_to_preserve: Preserve May 3, 2026 as the provenance for the EPS old raw and its Austrian-customer/EUR/40-business-location, single-use, no-standard-dispute, no-recurring, no-manual-capture, six-step redirect and 180-day refund statements (old raw lines 1-2, 8-12, 14-99, 113-156). The November capture documents many of these again (new raw lines 5-15, 18-68, 80-84, 113-137).

Preserve May's Invoicing invite-only footnote and shared bank-redirects matrix as dated wording rather than erase either or present them as present eligibility; the matrix lists EPS Subscriptions through send_invoice, not automatic charging (old raw lines 101-111; raw/stripe-bank-redirects-2025.md lines 24-34). November says Invoicing supported with a send_invoice-only footnote but recurring/off-session payments unsupported, so the captures cannot establish every account's entitlement or a general recurring charge route (new raw lines 42, 96-112).

Preserve May's diagram-based six-step flow and invite-only presentation as dated examples; November uses prose steps and broader matrices. A diagram/image removal is not evidence of a changed payment authorization contract (old raw lines 113-132; new raw lines 113-137; diff lines 196-226).
conflicts: Source-stripe-eps.md line 22, wiki/concepts/stripe-eps.md line 30, and wiki/concepts/stripe-bank-redirects.md line 34 state Invoicing invite-only based on May EPS raw line 111 and May bank-redirect raw lines 24-34; November's product matrix marks Invoicing supported with a send_invoice-only footnote at new raw lines 96-112. Date both claims and add reciprocal warnings to both concepts and the EPS source; neither absence of 'invite-only' in November nor the supported mark proves universal entitlement.

The older bank-redirect concept line 33 and source line 22 list EPS Subscriptions via send_invoice, following raw/stripe-bank-redirects-2025.md lines 24-34. November EPS raw line 42 labels recurring payments unsupported and lines 108-112 exclude setup_future_usage/off-session while marking an invoice collection footnote. Keep the per-invoice send_invoice route distinct from automated recurring charging and subscription-mode Checkout; record the dated scope tension without treating either label as proof of universal automatic payment support or cancellation of invoice collection.

The source line 24 and concept lines 16-21 label the six-step payment flow as if optional return is a confirmation step; November distinguishes immediate result from optional return (new raw lines 129-137), as May did (old raw lines 126-132). Preserve that distinction rather than treating browser return as payment success or payout.

Source line 19's absolute 'authentication prevents chargebacks' should track the narrower documented scope: EPS lacks the standard dispute/chargeback process, while bank customer contact can still route back to the merchant for refund (old raw lines 150-152; new raw lines 80-84).
unresolved_questions: Whether the November Invoicing supported mark means the prior invitation gate was lifted for all accounts, and precisely which product row the send_invoice footnote qualifies, is not settled by these captures (old raw lines 101-111; new raw lines 96-112).

The page does not verify a specific account's EPS capability, cross-border settlement currency, website review result, bank acceptance, payment outcome, bank-statement descriptor, refund completion time or actual customer receipt (new raw lines 18-40, 68-78, 129-143).

findings: Add November canonical/raw provenance while retaining the May capture and its dated 180-day/no-recurring/no-standard-dispute facts (source lines 4-8, 13-28; old raw lines 1-2, 32-54, 150-156; new raw lines 1-3, 41-68, 80-84).

Add the new 1.00 EUR minimum, account review and one-hour bank authorization as captured qualifications, keeping Austrian customer/EUR scope distinct from 40 supported business countries (source lines 13, 17, 21, 24; old raw lines 56-99, 113-132; new raw lines 16-40, 113-137).

Add non-cancelable separate-credit refund lifecycle, multiple partial refunds, 1–3-day typical bank timing without guaranteed maximum, Refund.status/webhook final outcomes and alternative method after failure; submission remains 180 days (source lines 13, 20; old raw lines 154-156; new raw lines 57-78).

Qualify the broader November product/API matrix and no off-session/setup_future_usage/SetupIntents support; source line 22's May Invoicing invite-only fact conflicts with November's supported mark and send_invoice footnote, so date both and reciprocally qualify direct EPS concept line 30 and shared bank-redirect concept line 34 (old raw lines 101-111; raw/stripe-bank-redirects-2025.md lines 24-34; new raw lines 86-112). The shared concept line 33's older Subscriptions via send_invoice wording is a per-invoice route, not proof of automatic recurring charging or Checkout subscription mode against November's recurring unsupported label at new raw line 42.
conflicts: May Invoicing invite-only at old raw line 111 and historical bank-redirect raw lines 24-34 underlies source line 22, direct concept line 30 and shared bank-redirect concept line 34, while November marks Invoicing supported and gives a send_invoice-only footnote at new raw lines 96-112; exact account entitlement and footnote attachment remain uncertain.

Shared bank-redirect concept line 33 and source line 22 preserve EPS Subscriptions via send_invoice from the May matrix (raw/stripe-bank-redirects-2025.md lines 24-34), whereas November EPS says recurring payments unsupported and excludes off-session at new raw lines 42, 105-112. Keep the older per-invoice route dated and distinct from automatic recurring charges and subscription-mode Checkout.

source_assessments.reason: The core EPS redirect and 180-day refund facts remain, but November adds material eligibility, minimum, authorization and refund-state details. Its Invoicing mark conflicts with undated May invite-only wording in the source and two concepts; the shared bank-redirects send_invoice subscription route also needs a dated per-invoice versus automated-recurring qualification.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/eps, the November capture describes a single-use Austrian customer bank redirect in EUR, with Stripe accounts in 40 listed business locations, merchant and Connect eligibility, B2B/B2C and cross-border classification, a 1.00 EUR minimum, possible account review and no recurring/manual-capture support (new raw lines 5-65). The customer chooses a bank, authenticates there within one hour, sees an immediate result and may optionally return to the business; immediate notification and standard payout are distinct states, and browser return is no proof of settled funds (new raw lines 113-137). The May capture had the same core Austrian/EUR/redirect, no-recurring, 40-business-location and 180-day-refund model, but omitted the new minimum and authorization window (old raw lines 8-12, 14-99, 113-156). source-stripe-eps.md captures those core facts but retains May-only provenance and an undated Invoicing invite-only statement despite November's supported/send_invoice wording (source lines 4-28; new raw lines 96-112).
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/eps, the substantive new documentation is the 1.00 EUR minimum, one-hour bank authorization window, possible eligibility review, explicit API/product limits and detailed refund lifecycle, including non-cancelability, separate bank credit, status webhooks and alternative refund after failure (new raw lines 16-78, 86-112, 113-137). The 180-day submission window, Austrian customer/EUR scope and lack of standard chargebacks remain aligned with May (old raw lines 14-54, 150-156; new raw lines 32-68, 80-84). The May invite-only Invoicing footnote conflicts with November's supported mark and send_invoice footnote; source-stripe-eps.md line 22, direct EPS concept line 30 and shared bank-redirects concept line 34 need reciprocal dated warnings, with exact account entitlement and footnote attachment unresolved (old raw lines 101-111; raw/stripe-bank-redirects-2025.md lines 24-34; new raw lines 96-112). The older shared concept line 33 lists EPS Subscriptions via send_invoice; that per-invoice collection route must be distinguished from November's recurring payments unsupported label and off-session/setup_future_usage exclusions, without inferring automatic charging or universal invitation removal (new raw lines 42, 105-112). The replacement of old flow diagrams with prose, expanded tables and pricing URL change are presentation/navigation differences, not payment success evidence (old raw lines 113-148; new raw lines 113-149). Distinguish front-end enablement from account eligibility, bank authorization/result from optional browser return and payout, and Billing/Invoicing send_invoice from subscription-mode Checkout or off-session recurring capability.
